aftermathEffects.text: Two re-rolls, each for a single die or a single result of the War's Aftermath.
+2 Influence for a Victory, +1 for a Draw or Defeat.
+2 Experience per model for a Victory, +1 for a Draw or Defeat.
One Hero that took part and was not removed as a casualty may use Healing Herbs (the item is removed): every Injury roll the company makes at the end of the game gets +1. Not cumulative.
A model removed as a casualty that took part may use its Wondrous Cram (the item is removed): it does not roll on the Injury chart and counts as having rolled the Full Recovery result.
The victorious company may apply +1 / -1 to its first Reinforcement roll in the War's Aftermath right after this match.
A company that scores all 6 Objective Markers may acquire a free piece of Equipment worth up to 2 Influence.
Each Leader that is not removed from the board earns one additional Experience Point.
A company that scores all Cargo earns 1 bonus Influence.
The winner of the scenario may apply +1 or -1 to the second die result the next time they roll on the Scenario Table, after both dice have been rolled.
The model in possession of the Relic at the end of the game gains the benefit of the Fortify Spirit Magical Power in their next game, even if they have no Will remaining.

againstTheOdds.text: The Battle Company with the lower rating may select Against the Odds bonuses after the roll on the Scenario Table was made, but before setting up. Each bonus adds its Rating to the company's rating, which must not exceed the opponent's as a result of these bonuses. The rating difference is checked before Against the Odds bonuses.

bonuses.name: Influence
bonuses.text: +2 Influence for Victory, +1 for Draw or Defeat.

bonuses.name: Experience
bonuses.text: +2 Experience per model for Victory, +1 per model for Draw or Defeat.

bonuses.name: Reroll
bonuses.text: Two rerolls that each can be used at any point during the game to re-roll a single die or the War's Aftermath for a single result.

bonuses.name: Tool Kit
bonuses.text: You may only have one of each Kit, but their items may be distributed to any members and ignore all capacity / alignment rules.

bonuses.name: Wanderer
bonuses.text: You may temporarily recruit a Wanderer for the match.

grants.rules: data.wanderers.rules (no Stand Fast, no Heroic Actions on the company, no Experience or Advancements)

budget.text: The sum of the Ratings of the chosen bonuses may not take the lower company above its opponent's Rating (equal is allowed: 'must not exceed'). So a bonus needs a Rating gap at least as large as its price: Ambush! needs a gap of 60 on its own.

eligible.text: Only the company with the lower Rating chooses; at equal Ratings nobody does. The comparison (and the 25 rating difference of the scenarios with an Attacker and a Defender) is made before Against the Odds bonuses.

scenarioExceptions.text: Models standing on the hill never take Courage tests for being Broken.
Defender models within 6" of the Gate pass every Courage test automatically.
The Defender's Baggage Ponies are not counted when working out its Break Point.
Neutral models never take Courage tests for being Broken.
Models that have not arrived yet count as being on the battlefield when checking whether the company is Broken.

gains.label: Wounding at least one enemy, even if it was subsequently prevented
Each enemy Hero or Monster they slay
Preventing a Wound by spending a Fate point
Rolling for and then passing a Courage test for being Broken
Carrying or being within range of an Objective at the end of the game (includes escaping off the board edge, controlling sections of the board, etc.)
Being declared MVP by the opposing player after the game

injuries.applies: Every model removed as a casualty (except models that fled the board) rolls on the chart for its type. Models that are Injured do not count towards the company's Rating.
injuries.deathOfAHero: If your Leader is slain, choose one of your Sergeants to be promoted to Leader after the battle. If you ever have less than two Sergeants, another Hero who is not already a Leader or Sergeant may become a Sergeant. If there is no Hero available, the Warrior with the most Experience Points is instantly treated as having rolled Hero in the Making on the Warrior Progression Chart (gaining Might, Will and Fate). Ties go to the highest Rating, then the controlling player.

healing.hero: Spend 1 Influence to attempt to remove an Injury from a Hero on a 5+ (the roll may be modified with additional Influence the same way as a Might point), or send the Hero to the healers: they miss the next game but remove one Injury from their profile.
healing.warrior: Spend 1 Influence to remove the Injured condition from a Warrior.

hero.name: Dead
hero.text: Your Hero's adventure ends here; no doubt their followers will mourn them. Remove the Hero, and all of their wargear, from your Battle Company Roster.

hero.name: Arm Wound
hero.text: From this point on, the Hero cannot benefit from a shield in any way, use a two-handed weapon, pike, or fire a bow or crossbow of any sort. They may still carry a Company Standard with the normal penalties and fight with a Hand Weapon. If the Hero would suffer a second Arm Wound, they will be forced to retire, as per the Dead result.

hero.name: Leg Wound
hero.text: The Hero has their Move value permanently reduced by 1". If the Hero would suffer a second Leg Wound, they will be forced to retire, as per the Dead result.

hero.name: Broken Honour
hero.text: The Hero has been shamed in battle, they may no longer provide a "Stand Fast!". Nor may they affect members of the Battle Company with their Heroic Actions. Should the Hero suffer this result a second time, they will gain the Fearful special rule. If the Hero would suffer a third Broken Honour, they will be forced to retire, as per the Dead result.

hero.name: T'is Just a Scratch
hero.text: They must miss the next game. Alternatively, the Hero may roll again on this chart - however, the second result will apply even if it is worse than the first. If this result should occur after any reroll, the Hero must miss the next game.

hero.name: Full Recovery
hero.text: The Hero may play in the next game as normal. Additionally, the Hero may heal one Arm Wound, Leg Wound, or Broken Honour they previously obtained. This resets the "count" that the specific Injury is giving them toward a forced retirement.

hero.name: Protection by the Valar
hero.text: The Hero is considered to have made a Full Recovery. Additionally, the Hero permanently gains +1 Fate point (to their Path's Maximum).

hero.name: Wounds of a Hero
hero.text: The Hero model's Battle Company immediately gains an extra D6 Influence Points; additionally, the Hero is considered to have made a Full Recovery.

retirement.text: A Hero that would suffer a retireAtCount-th occurrence of an injury is forced to retire, as per the Dead result: removed from the roster with all wargear.

rollModifier.text: A modifier (Healing Herbs +1) is added to the 2d6 total before the chart is read; a total above 12 reads as 12.

hero.text: Spend 1 Influence and roll a D6: on a 5+ remove one Injury, or the miss-next-game status of T'is Just a Scratch (the Hero then plays the next game). The roll may be raised with additional Influence, as with a Might point. A failed attempt loses the Influence; the player may try again, with no limit.
Send the Hero to the healers: no roll, the Hero misses the next game but removes one Injury.

warrior.text: Remove the Injured condition from a Warrior.

warrior.name: Dead
warrior.text: Remove the Warrior, and all their wargear, from the Company Roster.

warrior.name: Injured
warrior.text: The Warrior must miss the next game that your Battle Company participates in, but suffers no further effects.

warrior.name: Full Recovery
warrior.text: The Warrior makes a full recovery, and may fight in the next battle as normal.

warrior.name: Lesson Learned
warrior.text: The Warrior is considered to have made a Full Recovery. Additionally, the Warrior gains +D3 Experience.

matchInput.text: Per match the players enter, for each company: the roles, the Against the Odds bonuses, the Victory Points (from the scenario's scoringObjectives), whether the Battle Company fled, the scenario reward flags and, for every model, what happened to it and which experience gains it earned. The winner is the company with the most Victory Points; equal Victory Points are a draw (stated in the Objectives of most scenarios).

aftermath.rewards: campaign.aftermathEffects[] whose key is listed in the scenario's rewards[].effect, applied when its condition holds

gold.text: No scenario of the rulebook rewards Gold; Gold comes from the starting company and from the organiser (campaign.gold.sources).

perCompany.text: Attacker or Defender, for the scenarios that have roles.
The Against the Odds bonuses taken before setting up; they only apply to the lower rated company (campaign.aftermathEffects).
The total of the Victory Points scored; entered as a total or built up objective by objective.
One entry per scoring objective (tier, count or per-item tiers); 'side' limits an objective to the Attacker or the Defender.
The tickable conditions of the scenario rewards (companyFlag, modelFlag); the conditions victory and leaderNotRemoved are derived from the result and the model outcomes.
The Kits taken (one Tool Kit bonus each, no Kit twice); their items are then assigned to models.
The Wanderer that joins the company for this match only.
The scenario chosen with Ambush!, replacing the rolled one.
Models in the starting force (roster of the match, creatures, temporary Wanderer); the Break Point follows from it.
The turn at whose start the company became Broken, if it did.

All is Lost: the Broken company fled the battlefield; the opponent claims victory and full scenario rewards, the fleeing company keeps the participation Influence and Experience and its Against the Odds Influence and Experience bonuses, but no Win/Draw Influence and no scenario rewards.

perModel.text: A model removed as a casualty rolls on its Injury chart; a model that fled the board does not (campaign.injuries.applies). 'survived' covers every model still on the board at the end.
Every model that took part in the scenario; a model missing the game (Injured) is not in the match roster.
The item the model elects to use before the injury rolls (Healing Herbs: a Hero that was not a casualty; Wondrous Cram: a casualty); it is removed from the Equipment.

Carrying or being within range of an Objective at the end of the game (includes escaping off the board edge, controlling sections of the board, etc.)

options.label: Heroes may discard any wargear
options.description: Heroes may drop wargear that is part of their profile.

options.label: Path of Their Own Making (homebrew)
options.description: Units that are On Their Own Path level up on a homebrew path instead of staying warriors.

options.label: Shake the table
options.description: Throw the 3D dice with physics: one shake per roll.

options.label: Players may enter their own rolls
options.description: Let players type in the result of a roll instead of rolling in the app.

table.name: No Change
table.text: The Warrior does not gain a promotion.

table.name: Promoted
table.text: The Warrior has been granted a promotion by the leader of the company. Check the Advancements table on the company's page: the Warrior exchanges all characteristics and wargear for the new profile, while retaining any wargear that the new profile allows. A Warrior eligible for several promotions picks one. If there is no promotion, the Warrior increases Courage & Intelligence by +1 each, to a maximum of 3+.

table.name: A Hero in the Making
table.text: The Warrior is treated as a Hero and immediately gains 1 Might, Will, and Fate point. They retain their Experience Points and advance like a Hero from the next game on. Alternatively the model may forgo the Hero's Journey and take their Promotion instead.

exceptions.reason: Unique Wargear of the one company that lists it (Wood Elf Spear, 1 Influence); no other armoury sells it
'1 Ranger of the North with armour': the Armoury wargear table has no armour row, it only comes from the starting company
Sharkey's Rogues start with 'Ruffian with whip'; the Armoury sells no whip, only the company page exempts it from the Throwing Weapon limit
Harad's starting company and charts give Watchers of Kârna 'with Twin Blades'; the Armoury sells no Twin Blades

options.reason: a banner, war horn or war drum: the Battle Companies equipment sells the Company Standard, Company Horn and Company Drum instead, and a 'Choice of Options' excludes these options

rules.name: Combat Synergy
rules.definition: At the start of any phase, before the Declare Heroic Actions step, if this Hero and X are within 1" of each other then they can swap places with each other - this does not count as Moving. If they have used this special rule during a turn, then during the Fight Phase of that turn they may each re-roll a single D6 when making a Duel Roll.

rules.name: Poisoned Attacks
rules.definition:
A model with this special rule most re-roll any To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Shooting Attacks or making Strikes.
 Sometimes, a particular weapon will be described as benefiting from this special rule. When this is the case, only To Wound Roll made for that weapon will be able to re-roll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1.

rules.name: Well-aimed Shot
rules.definition: When making a shooting attack, the first time this model fails an In The Way Roll he may make an Intelligence Test. If the test is passed, the In The Way Roll will be successful instead.

rules.name: Spy

auras.tip: Whilst within 12" and in sight of the chosen enemy Hero, its Heroic Actions may be cancelled.

rules.definition: At the beginning of the game, after both sides have deployed, this Hero may choose one enemy Hero in your opponent's Company. Whilst this Hero is within 12" of, and has Line of Sight to, the chosen Hero, whenever the chosen Hero declares a Heroic Action they must roll a D6. On a 1-2, the Heroic Action is immediately cancelled and the Might Point is not spent. The chosen Hero may not then attempt to declare the same Heroic Action again that turn.

rules.name: Gatekeeper

auras.tip: May select one enemy Infantry model within 6" in sight.

rules.definition: At the end of the Priority Phase, this Hero may spend a Will Point to use this special rule. If they do, this Hero may select a single enemy Infantry model within 6" and Line of Sight and roll a D6. On a 3+, the chosen model may not Move during their Activation, but may otherwise act normally. Monster models are unaffected by this special rule.

rules.name: Heroic Move Mastery

auras.tip: Friendly Heroes within 6" gain a bonus on the roll-off for Heroic Moves.

rules.definition: If during the Declare Heroic Actions step of a Move Phase or Fight Phase, both sides have declared a Heroic Move or a Heroic Combat and a roll-off is required to see which side's Heroic Move happens first, friendly Heroes within 6" of this Hero will gain a bonus to that roll. If they would normally win the roll-off on a 4+, they will instead win it on a 3+. If they would normally win the roll-off on a 1, 2, or 3, they will instead win the roll-off on a 1, 2, 3, or 4.

rules.name: Longbeard
rules.definition: During the Priority Phase, after the roll for Priority has taken place, this Hero can spend a Will Point to allow their controlling player to re-roll their roll for Priority.

rules.name: Reading the Portents

auras.tip: Spend a Will Point to let a friendly model within 6" re-roll one Duel die.

rules.definition: During the Fight Phase, this Hero can spend a Will Point to allow a friendly model within 6" to re-roll a single die during their Duel Roll. This Hero can use this special rule multiple times during the same Fight Phase, so long as they have Will Points remaining.

rules.name: Big Game Hunter
rules.definition: If this Hero successfully Wound an enemy Monster model with a shooting attack (a Wound is caused and is not prevented), it will deal D3 Wounds rather than 1.

rules.name: Knife Mastery

auras.tip: Friendly models with a bow or crossbow within 3" in sight re-roll To Wound rolls of 1.

rules.definition: Friendly Battle Company models with any bow or crossbow within 3" and Line of Sight of this Hero may reroll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes. Additionally, friendly Battle Company models with any bow or crossbow within 3" and Line of Sight of this Hero may use the Shielding rule even if they do not possess any kind of shield.

rules.name: Heroic Shoot Mastery
rules.definition: When benefiting from a Heroic Shoot called by this Hero, friendly models may reroll failed To Wound Rolls when making shooting attacks.

rules.name: Swift Shot
rules.definition: This Hero never suffers the -1 penalty To Hit for Moving and Shooting. May fire a Crossbow after moving up to half of their Movement value, but with a -1 penalty.

rules.name: Rapid Fire
rules.definition: If this Hero hits a target with its ranged weapon in the Shoot Phase, it may make another shooting attack with its weapon that targets a model within 3" of the initial target - it may even be the same target. If that second shot also hits, then this model may Shoot again as described above. This model can make a maximum of three shots per turn as a result of this special rule.

rules.name: A Good Sort

auras.tip: Within 3" of another friendly Hero this Hero has +1 Attack.

rules.definition: Whilst within 3" of another friendly Hero, this Hero increases their Attacks by 1 and may re-roll any rolls of a 1 in this Hero's Duel rolls.

rules.name: Relentless Commander

auras.tip: If you give Priority to the opponent, friendly models within 6" re-roll To Wound rolls of 1.

rules.definition: Whilst this Hero is alive and on the battlefield, if you win the roll to choose who has Priority, and choose to give Priority to your opponent, then until the end of the turn friendly Battle Company models within 6" of this Hero may reroll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes.

rules.name: Heroic Combat Mastery
rules.definition: The Hero may call Heroic Combat without expending a point of Might if they slayed an enemy model they were Engaged in Combat with in the previous turn.

rules.name: Fearsome Charge
rules.definition: If this Hero Charges into Combat, then until the end of the turn they count as having the Terror special rule.

rules.name: Reckless Charge
rules.definition: If this Hero Charges into Combat, then must reroll failed To Wound rolls when making Strikes.

rules.name: Pinpoint Shot
rules.definition: Instead of shooting normally in the Shoot Phase, this Hero may make a single shooting attack against an enemy model Engaged in Combat with a friendly model (including himself). If they do, then if the To Hit Roll is successful, this Hero doesn't need to make any In The Way Rolls – the shot will automatically hit its target.

rules.name: "Hold positions, loose the arrows!"

auras.tip: Friendly models within 3" re-roll failed To Hit rolls when they shoot, if they did not Move.

rules.definition: Whilst within 3" of this Hero, friendly models may re-roll failed To Hit Rolls when making a shooting attack, providing they didn't Move in the preceding Move Phase.

rules.name: Heroic Accuracy Mastery
rules.definition: Friendly models benefiting from this Hero's Heroic Accuracy pass in-the-way checks on a 2+ rather than 4+.

rules.name: Volley Fire
rules.definition: This Hero increases the range of their shooting attacks by 6", provided they have not moved that turn. This special rule does not apply to throwing weapons.

rules.name: Lethal Aim
rules.definition: Each turn during the Shoot Phase, this Hero gains a free Might Point that can only be spent during a shooting attack on either a To Hit Roll, a To Wound Roll, or an In The Way Test. If this free Might Point is not spent by the end of the turn, it is lost.

rules.name: Usurper of Kings
rules.definition: If this Hero is Engaged in Combat with an enemy Hero, this Hero may re-roll a single D6 during the Duel Roll. Additionally, this Hero must reroll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes against an enemy Hero.

rules.name: Claim the Throne

auras.tip: After the enemy Leader falls within 6" of this Hero, friendly models treat it as a banner with range 6".

rules.definition: If the enemy Leader is removed as a casualty whilst within 6" of this Hero, then for the duration of the battle friendly Battle Company models treat this Hero as a banner with a range of 6".

rules.name: Heroic Challenge Mastery
rules.definition: The number of bonus Attacks granted by the Heroic Challenge is increased to +2 for this Hero, rather than the normal +1.

rules.name: General Hunter
rules.definition: If this model slays the enemy General in a Combat, they immediately regain a single point of Might spent earlier in the battle.

rules.name: Cunning Fighter
rules.definition: If this Hero wins a Duel Roll, and there are no other allies involved in the Combat (including Supporting models) then this Hero can choose a single enemy model on a 25mm base that he was Engaged in Combat with and roll a D6. On a 4+, the chosen model is knocked Prone before Strikes are made.

rules.name: Deceptive Caster
rules.definition: At the beginning of the game, after both sides have deployed, this Hero may choose a single enemy Hero. The chosen Hero suffers a -1 penalty to any Resist Tests they take when targeted by a Magical Power Cast by this Hero; except any natural 6.

rules.name: Heroic Channeling Mastery
rules.definition: When the Hero casts a Heroic Channeled spell that targets a single model, they may target one additional model.

rules.name: Sorcerous Adept
rules.definition: Each time this Hero rolls one or more natural 6s when making a Casting Test, they will regain a single Will Point after resolving the effects of the Magical Power.

rules.name: Master of Magic
rules.definition: This Hero may still be Activated whilst Engaged in Combat in order to attempt to Cast Magical Powers whilst Engaged in Combat, with the exception of the following Magical Powers: Nature's Wrath, Sorcerous Blast, Call Winds, and Tremor.

rules.name: Swift Parry
rules.definition: This Hero may force one enemy model involved in the same Combat as them to re-roll a single D6 for their Duel Roll. This must be done before all other re-rolls, and before any Might Points are spent.

rules.name: Marshal
rules.definition: This Hero and friendly Battle Company Warriors that can draw Line of Sight to this Hero may re-roll any failed Intelligence Tests and gain the Shieldwall special rule.

rules.name: Heroic Defence Mastery
rules.definition: The Hero may call Heroic Defence without expending Might if they are outnumbered in Combat.

rules.name: Defender of the City
rules.definition: This Hero may use the Shielding special rule even if they are not armed with a shield. If this Hero elects to shield, and wins the ensuing Combat, they may make a single Strike against one enemy model that was involved in the Combat.

rules.name: The King's Protector

auras.tip: The chosen Hero engaged within 6" gets a free Heroic Combat from this Hero.

rules.definition: At the start of the game, choose one friendly Battle Company Hero. If the target Hero is Engaged in Combat and within 6" of this Hero, this Hero may declare a Heroic Combat for free. If the Heroic Combat is successful then this Hero must use the following Move to join the target Hero's combat. If this is not possible, then this Hero must Move as close as possible to the target Hero.

rules.name: Experienced Tracker
rules.definition: At the start of each game, you may choose either Woodland Creature or Mountain Dwellers. Friendly Battle Company models gain the chosen special rule for the duration of the game.

rules.name: Heroic March Mastery
rules.definition: Models are not required to stay within the 'At the Double' range of this Hero in a turn in which this Hero declares a Heroic March.

rules.name: Chief Advisor

auras.tip: A friendly Hero within 6" that spends a Might Point rolls a D6: on a 6 it is free.

rules.definition: Whenever a friendly Battle Company Hero model within 6" spends a Might Point, they may roll a D6. On a natural 6, the Might Point is free and is not spent.

rules.name: Rallying Cry
rules.definition: Friendly Battle Company Infantry models can still charge after participating in a Heroic March called by this Hero.

rules.name: Furious Tirade

auras.tip: Enemy Warriors within 6" cannot use any Hero's Stand Fast.

rules.definition: Enemy Warrior models cannot benefit from a Hero model's Stand Fast whilst within 6" of this Hero.

rules.name: Commanding Bellow

auras.tip: Friendly models treat this Hero as a banner with range 3".

rules.definition: Friendly Battle Company models treat this Hero as a banner with a range of 3".

rules.name: Heroic Resolve Mastery
rules.definition: The Hero may call Heroic Resolve without expending Might if their force is Broken.

rules.name: Voice of Command

auras.tip: The Hero's Stand Fast reaches 12" instead of 6".

rules.definition: The range of this Hero's Stand Fast is 12" rather than 6". Additionally, friendly Hero models can benefit from this Hero's Stand Fast.

rules.name: Burly
rules.definition: A model with this special rule does not suffer the -1 penalty to the Duel Roll for using a two-handed weapon. Additionally, a model with this special rule can still Move its full Move Value whilst carrying a Heavy Object.

rules.name: To Arms!

auras.tip: Once per game friendly models within 3" get +1 Strength until the end of the turn.

rules.definition: Once per game, at the start of his Activation, this Hero can declare they are using this special rule. If they do, then until the end of the turn all friendly models within 3" of this Hero increase their Strength by 1.

rules.name: Heroic Strength Mastery
rules.definition: When this Hero declares a Heroic Strength, they may choose to make a single Strike against every enemy involved in the combat, including supporting models, instead of making Strikes as normal.

rules.name: Oblivious to Pain
rules.definition: Whenever this Hero suffers a Wound, roll a D6. On the roll of natural 6, the Wound is ignored.

rules.name: Fury of the Bear
rules.definition: If this Hero is involved in a Combat and kills every model he was Engaged in Combat with, then in the following turn he may declare a Heroic Move for free and must Charge if able.

rules.name: Grim Blade
rules.definition: This Hero will always win the roll-off during a Drawn Combat. If both sides have a Hero with this special rule, neither side will benefit from this special rule.

rules.name: For Glory

auras.tip: Once per game friendly models within 6" get +1 Fight and re-roll To Wound rolls of 1.

rules.definition: Once per game, at the start of any Fight Phase, this Hero can use this special rule so long as they are alive and on the battlefield. If they do, then friendly Battle Company models within 6" of this Hero gain a bonus of +1 Fight Value and may reroll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes until the end of the turn.

rules.name: Heroic Strike Mastery
rules.definition: When calling a Heroic Strike the Hero adds +3 to their Fight Value rather than rolling a D3.

rules.name: Master Duelist
rules.definition: At the start of a Combat involving this Hero, before any Heroic Strikes are resolved, this Hero may increase their Fight Value to match that of a single enemy model they are Engaged in Combat with.

rules.name: Warrior of Renown
rules.definition: Enemy models Engaged in Combat with this Hero cannot declare a Heroic Strike.

rules.name: The Charge of Gondor
rules.definition: This Hero gains a bonus of +1 to their Fight Value in a Combat in which they have charged.

rules.name: Remember Today

auras.tip: May use the Might, Will and Fate of another friendly Hero within 3".

rules.definition: This Hero may use the Might, Will, and Fate points of another friendly Hero within 3".

rules.name: Lord of Dol Amroth

auras.tip: Other friendly Dol Amroth models treat this Hero as a banner with range 6".

rules.definition: Other friendly Dol Amroth models treat this Hero as a banner with a range of 6".

rules.name: Lord of Lossarnach

auras.tip: Other friendly Lossarnach models within 3" re-roll To Wound rolls of 1.

rules.definition: Other friendly Lossarnach models within 3" of this Hero may re-roll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes.

rules.name: Chief of Lamedon

auras.tip: Other friendly Lamedon models within 3" pass their Courage Tests.

rules.definition: Other friendly Lamedon models within 3" of this Hero automatically pass any Courage Tests they are required to take.

rules.name: Lord of the Vale

auras.tip: Other friendly models within 3" re-roll To Hit rolls of 1 when they shoot, if they did not Move.

rules.definition: Other friendly models within 3" of this Hero may re-roll To Hit Rolls of a 1 when making a shooting attack in the Shoot Phase, provided they did not Move in the preceding Move Phase.

rules.name: Defiance
rules.definition: This Hero cannot have their Courage value reduced by enemy special rules or Magical Powers.

rules.name: Foresight of the Seer
rules.definition: Whenever this Hero suffers a Wound, roll a D6. On the roll of a natural 6, the Wound is ignored. If this Hero would later gain a special rule with the same effect (e.g. Oblivious to Pain) then treat that special rule as improving Foresight of the Seer to a natural 5+.

rules.name: There Were Some Who Resisted
rules.definition: The Hero may re-roll any dice that roll a 1 when making Courage Tests. Númenór Stands Alone! If you wish to represent Númenór by themselves, simply ignore any reference to Rivendell Warriors and use the Custom Selection Optional Rule to take exclusively Warriors of Númenór.

rules.name: Back on your Horses!
rules.definition: If the Hero started the scenario as a Cavalry model they may benefit from the following rule: At the end of this Hero's move, if they are in base contact with a friendly Cavalry Warrior model who is not Engaged in Combat, then the Warrior may give the Hero their horse. Replace the Warrior model with a suitable dismount, and replace the Hero with their original mounted version. The Warrior will be placed in the same place the Hero was, and vice versa. The Hero will only count as riding a standard horse after using this rule.

rules.name: One Final Blow
rules.definition: If this Hero is slain, they may immediately make one Strike on each enemy model that was Engaged with them using their base Strength.

rules.name: Know All Paths
rules.definition: This Hero and their Mount, if applicable, gain the Woodland Creature special rule.

rules.name: Lordly Quality
rules.definition: Friendly models that share the same faction keyword treat this Hero as a banner.

target.text: friendly models that share the bearer's faction keyword

rules.name: Defender
rules.definition: At the beginning of the Fight Phase, at the start of the Declare Heroic Actions step, if a friendly Hero with the opposite species keyword (Man/Dwarf) would be considered Trapped and is in a different Combat than this Hero, then this Hero may declare a Heroic Combat for free. If this Heroic Combat is successful, then this Hero must use the following Move to join the other's Combat. If not possible, then this Hero must Move as close as possible to each other.

target.text: a friendly Hero with the opposite species keyword (Man/Dwarf)

rules.name: Blessing of the Golden Wood
rules.definition: The Hero may re-roll any failed Fate rolls.

rules.name: Veteran of the Old Wars
rules.definition: This Hero gains the Terror special rule.

rules.name: Bladelord
rules.definition: If they are Outnumbered in a Combat, this Hero may reroll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes. If they have the Infantry keyword and are Outnumbered in a Combat, this Hero may instead re-roll all failed To Wound Rolls when making Strikes.

rules.name: The Stubbornness of Dwarves
rules.definition: During a Duel roll, before any rerolls are used, if the opposing player rolled more dice in the combat then the Hero may reroll a single d6 as part of the Duel roll.

rules.name: Stubborn Brilliance!
rules.definition: The Hero gains the Master of Battle (5+) special rule.

rules.name: Moneybags

auras.tip: Friendly Lake-town models within 6" get +1 Fight and treat this Hero as a banner.

rules.definition: At the start of the Fight phase, before any Heroic Actions are declared, the Hero can spend a Will Point to use this special rule. If he does, then any friendly Lake-town models within 6" of this Hero gains a bonus of +1 to their Fight Value and treats this Hero as a banner until the end of the turn.

rules.name: You Have My Sword

auras.tip: A Hobbit engaged within 6" lets this Hero declare a free Heroic Combat.

rules.definition: During the Declare Heroic Actions step of the Fight Phase, if a friendly Hobbit is Engaged in Combat and is within 6" of this Hero, this Hero may declare a free Heroic Combat. If this Heroic Combat is successful, then this Hero must use the following Move to join the Hobbit's Combat. If this is not possible, then this Hero must Move as close as possible to the Hobbit. This Hero cannot use this special rule if they are engaged in the same Combat as the Hobbit in question.

rules.name: I Have My Own Sword, Thank You Very Much
rules.definition: This model may re-roll any failed To Wound rolls when making Strikes.

rules.name: Of a Party Sort
rules.definition: The Hero will pass a Fate Roll on a 3+ rather than a 4+. Additionally, the Hero may re-roll failed Fate Rolls.

rules.name: Throwing Stones
rules.definition: Instead of using the Throw Stones special rule as normal, the Hero may use stones in the same way as a Throwing Weapon. These have a Strength of 1 and a range of 8", and the Hero may re-roll any failed To Wound Rolls when using stones as a Throwing Weapon.

rules.name: Orcish Brawler
rules.definition: If this Hero is outnumbered during a Fight then they gain a bonus of +1 to their Attacks value for the duration of the Combat.

rules.name: Animosity
rules.definition: If the Hero is an Orc, they gain a bonus of +1 To Wound whilst a friendly Uruk-hai is engaged in the same combat. If the Hero is an Uruk-hai, they gain a bonus of +1 To Wound whilst a friendly Orc is engaged in the same combat.

rules.name: She Hungers for Sweeter Meats
rules.definition: This Hero adds 1 to their Attacks characteristic whilst they are Engaged in Combat with an enemy Man, Elf, Dwarf or Hobbit model.

rules.name: Morgul Weaponry
rules.definition: Each time this Hero inflicts an unsaved Wound on an enemy model, roll a D6. On a 5+, that model suffers an additional Wound (Fate may still be used as normal).

rules.name: Show of Strength
rules.definition: If this Hero slays one or more enemy models in Combat, then for the duration of the following turn they gain a bonus of +1 to their Fight Value.

rules.name: Pillager
rules.definition: The Hero gains +1 to Wound when making Strikes whilst within 3" of an Objective Marker, static or otherwise.

rules.name: There will be no dawn for Men
rules.definition: The Hero gains the Hatred (Man) special rule.

rules.name: Savage Charge
rules.definition: The Hero still gains the Extra Attack bonus even when they Charge a Cavalry model, and will retain it even if they are subsequently Charged by a Cavalry model.

rules.name: Feral Charge
rules.definition: When the Hero Charges an enemy Infantry model, they gain the Knock to the Ground bonus as if they were Cavalry. This bonus is lost if they are subsequently Charged by an enemy Cavalry model.

rules.name: Whipped into a Frenzy
rules.definition: Whenever this Hero suffers a Wound, roll a D6. On the roll of a natural 6, the Wound is ignored. If this Hero would later gain a special rule with the same effect (e.g. Oblivious to Pain) then treat that special rule as improving Whipped into a Frenzy to a natural 5+.

rules.name: Strength in Numbers
rules.definition: The Hero gains the Backstabbers special rule.

rules.name: Callous Leadership

auras.tip: Friendly Goblins within 3" get +1 To Wound; one that loses a Duel risks a wound.

rules.definition: At the start of the Fight Phase, before Heroic Actions are declared, the Hero may spend a Will Point to use this special rule. All friendly Goblin models within 3" gain a +1 To Wound when making Strikes. However, any friendly Goblin model within 3" that loses a Duel roll (including supporting models) must roll a D6 after any Strikes have been made. On a 1, the model suffers a Wound.

rules.name: Cover of Darkness
rules.definition: As part of this Hero's activation, they may spend a Will point and declare they are using this ability. Until the End Phase, the Fighting at Night special rules will be in play. (see page 137 of the Middle- earth Strategy Battle Game Rules Manual)

rules.name: Master of Poisons
rules.definition: This Hero must re-roll all failed To Wound rolls.

rules.name: Seize Command

auras.tip: When the Leader has one Wound left within 3" in sight, it may be removed to give this Hero command.

rules.definition: If during the End Phase of any turn your Leader has only a single Wound remaining and is within 3" and Line of Sight of this Hero, you may choose to remove your Leader as a casualty. If you do, this Hero immediately assumes the role of "Leader" for the purposes of Victory Points instead. Do not make an Injury roll for models removed in this way. This model cannot use this special rule on itself.

rules.name: Skilled Blade
rules.definition: When fighting an enemy Hero, this Hero may force their opponent to reroll one of their dice in the Duel roll. This is not cumulative with other special rules that confer the same effect.

rules.name: Master Skirmisher
rules.definition: The Hero may still fire a bow even if they have moved over half their Move value this turn. If the Hero fires a Blowpipe or a Throwing Weapon, they instead do not suffer the -1 penalty for moving. Additionally, the Hero does not suffer the -1 penalty for using a two-handed weapon in a turn in which they Charged.

rules.name: Master Hunter
rules.definition: This Hero does not suffer any penalties for Moving through Difficult Terrain. Additionally, they may still gain the bonuses for Charging whilst in Difficult Terrain if they have the Cavalry keyword.

rules.name: Swap with Me!

auras.tip: May swap places with a friendly Goblin on a 25mm base within 3".

rules.definition: At the start of the Fight Phase, before the Declare Heroic Actions Step, the Hero can choose a friendly Goblin model on a 25mm base within 3"and swap places with it. This does not count as Moving.

rules.name: Feel no Pain
rules.definition: Whenever this Hero suffers a Wound, roll a D6. On the roll of a natural 5+, the Wound is ignored.

rules.name: Command Support
rules.definition: A keyword some equipment (a War Drum, a War Horn, a Pennant, an Instrument) gives its bearer to stand for the leader's command retinue. It has no effect in play: a few scenarios score Victory Points for Command Support models still alive at the end of the game.

rules.name: Laden with Baggage
rules.definition: A Baggage Pony has a carrying capacity of up to 15 pieces of Equipment, weapons or additional wargear (except mounts). Whilst these pieces are on the Packhorse, the company gains no benefit from them. During the War's Aftermath, after determining injuries but before determining the next scenario, any member of a Battle Company may retrieve, store, or swap one of its pieces of Wargear or Equipment for an item from the Pony. During a scenario, any member of a Battle Company that begins its turn in base contact with the Pony may do likewise. Note that your Battle Company must still abide by the Wargear Limits at all times and each member must follow restrictions for Warriors and Heroes as normal.

rules.name: Keen Sight (Falcon)
rules.label: Keen Sight

auras.tip: Enemy models within 12" gain no benefit from Stalk Unseen (a Falcon apart from its Hero).

rules.definition: Enemy models within 12" of a Falcon that is separate from its Hero may not benefit from the Stalk Unseen special rule.

rules.name: Handler's Glove

auras.tip: The Hero may release its creature anywhere within 3".

rules.definition: This Creature starts the game upon the arm of its master rather than on the board. At the start of any turn in which the Creature is on their Hero model's arm, the Hero may release the creature - place it anywhere within 3" of the Hero. Whilst separate from its Hero, the Creature may move independently. If, during the End phase of any turn, a Creature is within 3" of their Hero, it may choose to land back on their Hero model's arm. Remove the Creature from the board. Whilst upon the Hero model's arm, the Creature cannot be targeted, attacked or hit with shooting attacks, and will not provide an In The Way roll for their Hero.

rules.name: A fell light is in them

auras.concept: A fell light is in them
auras.tip: At the end of its Move may choose one enemy model within 12" in sight.

rules.definition:
At the end of this model's Move, it can choose a single enemy model within 12" and Line of Sight. The chosen model must take an Intelligence Test. If the test is failed, you may Move the chosen model up to its Move Value directly towards this model, even if it has already Moved that turn.
 The chosen model will stop Moving if it would enter the Control Zone of an enemy model (with the exception of this model), If it comes into contact with an Obstacle, another model (though they will never count as Charging in this instance, and therefore cannot be involved in Combat with the model) or piece of impassable terrain, or if the model reaches the edge of a cliff or other such edge that would cause it to take falling damage.
 This Move cannot be used to move a Model out of Combat, make a model dismount, drop an item, or Lie Down. However, if the Move would allow the chosen model to Charge this model, then this model may make them Charge. A model affected by this special rule cannot Move any further that turn, and may not use Active abilities.

rules.name: At Path's End
rules.definition: This unit earns no Experience Points and cannot level up (no progression, no promotion, no Hero in the Making).

rules.name: Whirl of Attacks
rules.definition: When rolling a natural 6 for their Duel Roll, this Hero rolls an additional attack when rolling to Wound. This rule cannot be used if the enemy model is Trapped.

rules.name: Master of Fighting Styles
rules.definition: The Hero has mastered different fighting styles. Before the Duel Roll, this Hero may use the rules for a two-handed weapon or shielding, even without the equipment.

rules.name: I shall pass!
rules.definition: If this Hero wins their Duel Roll, after all models have Backed Away but before making Strikes, this Hero may make no Strikes and instead Move again up to half their Move Value. If they Charge an enemy, they fight as normal. This rule can only be used once per turn. (Inspired by the Barge Brutal Power attack, for unclarities check page 90 of the Rules Manual.)

rules.name: Hatred
rules.definition: A model with this special rule gains a bonus of +1 To Wound when making Strikes against a model with the same keyword as the one shown in brackets. So, a model with the Hatred (Man) special rule would gain a bonus of +1 To Wound when making Strikes against Man models.

rules.name: Ancient Enemies
rules.definition: A model with this special rule re-rolls 1s To Wound when fighting in combat against models with the keywords listed in the brackets in its profile. For example, a model that has the Ancient Enemies (Elf) special rule will get to re-roll 1s To Wound against all Elf models

rules.name: Master of Battle

auras.tip: When an enemy Hero within 6" declares a Heroic Action, roll a D6 to copy it.

rules.definition: Whenever an enemy Hero declares a Heroic Action within 6" of this model, this model may roll a D6. If the result on the dice equals or beats the number shown in brackets, then this model may Immediately declare a Heroic Action of the same type without spending a Might Point. This may still be done if this model has no Might Points remaining or would not normally be able to declare that Heroic Action. If the roll is failed, this model may still declare a Heroic Action if they wish (though not one they cannot usually declare) for the usual cost of a Might Point.

rules.name: Dominant
rules.definition:
This model counts as the number of models as shown in brackets when working out how many models are in range of an objective, in a specific are of the board, or when working out how many models have escaped the battlefield. So, a model with Dominant (3) would count as three models in range of an objective, or in a specific are of the board, or three models when working out how many models have excaped the battlefield. If a model would gain this special rule whilst in range of another model or specific area of the board, and then moves off the board, they will not gain the benefit of this special rule once off the board.
 If a model has two sources of the Dominant (X) special rule, then they use the highest value.

rules.name: Fury

auras.tip: While in effect, friendly models within 6" with the keywords in brackets pass Courage Tests.

rules.definition: This Magical Power targets the caster. Friendly models within 6" of the caster who have the same keywords as those shown in brackets will automatically pass any Courage Tests they are required to take.

target.text: friendly models with the {X} keywords within 6"

rules.name: Terror
rules.definition:
If a model wishes to Charge a model with this special rule, then it must take a Courage Test at the start of its Move. If the test is passed, the model may Charge as normal. If the test is failed, the model cannot Move that turn, but may otherwise act normally.
 Sometimes a situation may open up the chance for a model to Charge a model with Terror part way through their Move, such as moving a different model with magic or killing something in the way with a throwing weapon. In such instances, the model only needs to take the Courage Test at the point in which the Terror causing model becomes possible to Charge. If a model making a Jump, Climb or Leap Test finishes within the Control Zone of an enemy with Terror and would normally be able to Charge, they will take their Courage Test after they have made their Jump, Climb or Leap Test.
 Sometimes, a model may only cause Terror In certain enemies. In these Instances, a keyword will follow Terror in brackets, and only models with that keyword will need to take a Courage Test to Charge the model. So, a model with Terror (Orc) will only cause Terror In Orc models, When the rule is shown with a keyword in brackets (e.g. the Torching Brand's Terror (Beast) and Terror (Cavalry)), it only affects models that have that keyword.

auras.tip: The Heroic March shout: friendly models within 6" of the Hero's start add to their Move and must end within 6".
Friendly models within 6" get an extra free die on Resist Tests until the End Phase.

auras.label: Take Aim

After slaying 3 enemy Heroes or Monsters, other friendly Orcs and Trolls treat this model as a banner with range 6".
Names an enemy Hero within 6" of the same Heroic Tier or higher.

magic.castingRule: A Casting Value is the dice score needed on a D6 for a Casting Test (a 4+ Power needs a 4, 5 or 6). Improving it by 1 lowers it by 1 (5+ becomes 4+); a Power can be improved at most twice. Magical Powers and Casting Value improvements add no rating.

gear.name: Spear
gear.definition: Support: an Infantry model with it that is not Engaged in Combat can assist a friendly model in base contact whose base is the same size or smaller. It adds one dice (its own Fight Value) to that Combat's Duel Roll and, if its side wins, makes one Strike with its own Strength. A Supporting model is not involved in the Combat (cannot be struck). It Supports one Combat per Fight Phase and cannot Support if Prone, unable to Activate, or if it shot that turn. It is a hand weapon when the model is Engaged.

gear.definition: Two-handed weapon: -1 to the Duel Roll (not on a natural 6) and +1 to To Wound rolls when making Strikes.

If they do, choose a single enemy model involved in the Combat. This model and the chosen model both roll a single D6 and add their Strength characteristic. If this model rolls equal to or higher than the chosen model, then the chosen model is immediately knocked Prone. This may be done before any other friendly models make their strikes. Two-handed weapon: -1 to the Duel Roll (not on a natural 6) and +1 to To Wound rolls when making Strikes.

gear.definition: Adds 1 to Defence, but not if the model also has a bow, crossbow, two-handed weapon or pike (or uses a hand-and-a-half weapon two-handed in that Combat). Shielding (Active): at the start of a Combat, before the Duel Roll, the model may double its Attacks for that Combat; if it wins it cannot Strike and gets no benefit from its weapons' special rules. In a Multiple Combat all friendly models must Shield or none can; a Shielding model cannot be Supported; Cavalry cannot Shield; a Prone model can.

In these instances, a Good model armed with an Elven weapon will win the roll-off on a 3+, whilst an Evil model armed with an Elven weapon will win the roll-off on a 1-4. If both sides have an Elven weapon, neither side gains the benefit. Some Missile Weapons may also be classed as Elven weapons; however, the above bonus only applies to Melee Weapons.

scenarios.name: Seize Ground
scenarios.description: As two companies become locked in a battle of wits and cunning, it becomes apparent that victory can only be seized by claiming key areas of the battlefield. As both leaders rally their followers, a fight for control of the battlefield is about to begin.
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65. Then, place five Objective Markers on the battlefield; one is automatically placed in the centre of the board. To place the other objectives, both players roll a D6. The player with the highest score places one objective anywhere on the battlefield at least 12" away from the existing objective and 6" away from any board edge. Their opponent then places a third objective at least 12" away from existing objectives and at least 6" away from any board edge. The players then alternate placing the remaining two objectives, according to the restriction noted earlier.
scenarios.objectives: The game lasts until the end of a turn in which one Army has been reduced to a quarter (25%) of its starting number of models or below, at which point the player that has scored the most Victory Points wins the game. If both players have the same number of Victory Points, the game is a draw.

options.text: For each Objective Marker, you score 1 Victory Point if you have more models within 3" than your opponent.
If you have at least twice as many models as your opponent within 3", you instead score 2 Victory Points.
If you are the only player to have models within 3", you instead score 3 Victory Points.
You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Leader was wounded during the game.
If the enemy Leader was removed as a casualty, you instead score 2 Victory Points.
You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Battle Company is Broken at the end of the game.
If the enemy Battle Company is Broken and your Battle Company is not, you instead score 3 Victory Points.

scenarios.startingPositions:
Both players roll a D6, with the highest scoring player choosing their table edge. They then select a model of their Battle Company, and any attached Creatures, to deploy wholly within 12" of their board edge. Creatures must be deployed within 6" of their owner.

When this has been done, the opposing player chooses one of their models and deploys it in similar fashion. Players then alternate until all models have been placed.

scenarios.name: Chance Encounter
scenarios.description: Upon their travels through Middle-earth, two opposing Battle Companies have happened upon each other. A company that is seemingly alone, and with no support in sight, is not an opportunity to pass up lightly. As the companies engage, a solid tactical mind and skill at arms will see victory won.
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65.
scenarios.objectives: The game lasts until the end of a turn in which one Battle Company has been reduced to 25% of its starting models, at which point the player who has scored the most Victory Points wins the game. If both players have the same number of Victory Points, the game is a draw.

rewards.name: Rendezvous
rewards.text: The victorious Battle Company may apply +1 / -1 to their first Reinforcement roll in the subsequent War's Aftermath.

options.text: You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Leader was wounded during the game.

If the enemy Leader was removed as a casualty, you instead score 5 Victory Points.
You score 3 Victory Points if the enemy Battle Company is Broken at the end of the game.
If the enemy Battle Company is Broken and your Battle Company is not, you instead score 5 Victory Points.
You score 2 Victory Points if your opponent has no Company Support remaining at the end of the game.
You score 1 Victory Point if you have at least one Command Support remaining at the end of the game.
If you have more Command Support alive than your opponent, then you instead score 2 Victory Points.
You score 3 Victory Points if the enemy Battle Company has been reduced to 25% of its starting models at the end of the game.

scenarios.name: Secure the Area
scenarios.description: Hidden somewhere upon the battlefield lies something of great value to both sides. Whether this is a hoard of treasure, the entrance to a secret passageway, the fallen body of an ally or even something much more valuable; both sides must strive to claim it and defend it at all costs.

scenarios.objectives:
Once one Battle Company has been Broken, the game might suddenly end. At the end of each turn after this condition has been met, roll a D6. On the result of 1-2, the game ends – otherwise, the battle continues for another turn!

At the end of the game, the player who has scored the most Victory Points wins the game. If both players have the same number of Victory Points, the game is a draw.

rewards.text: The winner of the scenario has acquired a strategic advantage for their next battle. The next time they roll on the Scenario Table, after both dice have been rolled, they may apply a +1 or -1 to the second die result.

specialRules.name: Supply Markers
specialRules.definition:
The Objective Markers represent a series of supplies that both sides are trying to destroy. To attempt to destroy an enemy Supply Marker, a model must be standing and in base contact with the marker during the End Phase of a turn having not Cast any Magical Powers, used a Missile Weapon, been Engaged in Combat, Supported a Combat, been rendered unable to Move any further that turn due to a special rule or result of a test (such as a Thrown Rider Test) or been under the effects of an enemy Magical Power that turn.

If the model in question has a Flaming Brand, Torch, or Torching Brand then they simply need to be standing and in base contact during the End Phase. The marker will then automatically be destroyed.

Both players roll a D6, with the highest scoring player choosing their table edge. They then select a model of their Battle Company, and any attached Creatures, to deploy wholly within 12" of their board edge. Creatures must be deployed within 6" of their owner.

When this has been done, the opposing player chooses one of their models and deploys it in similar fashion. Players then alternate until all models have been placed.

scenarios.name: Fog of War
scenarios.description: Two rival Battle Companies have stumbled upon each other in the act of delivering critical information to their allies. Each company is then locked in a battle of wits, both trying to outsmart the enemy..
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65.
scenarios.objectives:
Once one Battle Company has Broken, the game might suddenly end. At the end of each turn once this condition has been met, roll a d6. On a 3+, the game continues. If the roll is 1 or 2, the game ends.

At the end of the game, the player who has scored the most Victory Points wins the game. If both players have the same number of Victory Points, the game is a draw.

In this scenario, you do not have to reveal any objectives that you have achieved until the end of the game, and are in fact encouraged to keep them secret from your opponent.

Part of the skill involved is trying to work out what your opponent is attempting to accomplish while deceiving them in equal measure.

scoring.instruction: At the start of the game, secretly note down one of your own Hero models – this may not be your Leader unless you only have one Hero.

options.text: You score 1 Victory Point if the nominated Hero is still alive at the end of the game.
If the nominated Hero is still alive and has suffered no Wounds, you instead score 3 Victory Points.
If the nominated Hero is still alive and has suffered no Wounds, and spent no Fate Points, you instead score 5 Victory Points.

scoring.instruction: At the start of the game, secretly note down one of your opponent's Hero models – this may not be your opponent's Leader unless they only have one Hero.

options.text: You score 1 Victory Point for causing one or more Wounds on the nominated Hero. Wounds prevented by a successful Fate roll do not count.
If the nominated Hero has been removed as a casualty, you instead score 3 Victory Points.
If the nominated Hero has been removed as a casualty as a result of one of your models wounding them in Combat, you instead score 5 Victory Points.

scoring.instruction: At the start of the game secretly note down a single terrain piece wholly within your opponent's half of the board.

options.text: You score 1 Victory Point if at the end of the game you have more models than your opponent on or in base contact with your chosen terrain piece.
If at the end of the game, you have at least two models and twice as many as your opponent on or in base contact with your chosen terrain piece, you instead score 3 Victory Points.
If your opponent has no models on or in base contact with your chosen terrain piece and you have at least two, you instead score 5 Victory Points.
You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Leader was wounded during the game.
If the enemy Leader was removed as a casualty, you instead score 2 Victory Points.

scenarios.name: Show of Strength
scenarios.description: Two Battle Companies have clashed upon a battlefield, engaging in open war. The two leaders must show their skill and strength now more than ever, inspiring their followers to fight on in the face of adversity. Whichever leader can slay the most will no doubt win the day.
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65.
scenarios.objectives:
Whichever leader can slay the most will be the victor. Note that if your leader is missing this game, use the Sergeant in your Battle Company with the highest points cost instead.

The game lasts until the end of a turn in which one Battle Company has been reduced to 25% of its starting models.

options.text: You score 4 Victory Points if your Leader has killed more models than your opponent's Leader.
If your Leader has killed twice as many models as your opponent's Leader, then you instead score 8 Victory Points.
If your Leader has killed three times as many models as your opponent's Leader, or you are the only player to have a Leader that has killed models, then you instead score 12 Victory Points.
You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Leader was wounded during the game.
If the enemy Leader was wounded by your Leader, you instead score 3 Victory Points.
If the enemy Leader is slain by your Leader, you instead score 5 Victory Points.
You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Battle Company is Broken at the end of the game.
If the enemy Battle Company is Broken and your Battle Company is not, you instead score 3 Victory Points.

specialRules.name: The Last Stand
specialRules.definition: Each time a Leader slays an enemy Hero or multi-wound model, they regain a Might point spent earlier in the battle.

When this has been done, the opposing player chooses one of their models and deploys it in similar fashion. Players then alternate until all models have been placed.

scenarios.name: Scavenge the Battlefield
scenarios.description: The battlefield has seen several skirmishes before, and there appears to still be quite a number of valuable trinkets or items scattered around. Seeing this, both Battle Companies spring into action, attempting to secure as much wealth as they can.
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65. You then place the objective markers as shown on the map.
scenarios.objectives: Whichever Battle Company can hold the most objectives will be the winner. The game lasts until the end of a turn in which one Battle Company has been reduced to 25% of its starting models.

rewards.name: To the Victor Goes the Spoils
rewards.text: At the end of the scenario, if one company scores all 6 Objective Markers then they may acquire a free piece of Equipment worth up to 2 Influence Points.

options.text: For each Objective Marker your Battle Company has in its possession, you score 2 Victory Points.
If an Objective Marker isn't currently held, but you have more models within 3" of it than your opponent, you score 1 Victory Point.

If the enemy Leader was slain, you instead score 3 Victory Points.

If you have more Command Support alive than your opponent, then you instead score 2 Victory Points.

specialRules.name: Objectives
specialRules.definition: The six objectives on the board are Light Objects, as detailed on page 134 of the main rules manual. This means that models may pick up and carry the objectives; in fact, a model will only count as holding an objective once they have picked it up. If a model holding an objective flees, it is immediately dropped where they stood before they fled, or as close as possible. Models may carry more than one objective.

scenarios.name: Relic of Ages Past
scenarios.description: A relic of a bygone age has awoken, drawing all manner of armies and creatures to its power. The leaders of two rival Battle Companies desire it, either to progress their own standing, or to fulfil the task they have been set to reclaim it by their lord or commander – no matter the cost, both must claim it.
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout:
Set up terrain as described on page 65. Then, place six identical Objective markers on the battlefield where one is secretly marked as different from the others. All six Objective Markers should be identical on one side, with the one side that is the Relic clearly marked on the reverse side. To deploy the Objective Markers, place one exactly 12" from the centre of the northern edge and another exactly 12" from the centre of the southern board edge. The remaining four objectives are deployed so that they form a hexagon with each being 12" away from the others, as shown on the map.

It is recommended to have the campaign organizer or another player deploy the Objective Markers.
scenarios.objectives: The Battle Companies are searching for the relic, and once it is found, they must escape with it in their grasp. The game lasts until either the relic has been moved off of one board edge, or one side has been reduced to a quarter (25%) of their starting forces.

rewards.name: A Final Blessing
rewards.text: The model in possession of the Relic at the end of the game gains the benefit of the Fortify Spirit Magical Power in their next game, even if they have no Will remaining.

condition.label: In possession of the Relic at the end of the game

options.text: You score 8 Victory Points if your force is in possession of the relic at the end of the game.
If at the end of the game you are not in possession of the relic but have more models within 3" of the relic than your opponent, you instead score 4 Victory Points.

scoring.item: Objective Marker revealed to be a decoy

You score 1 Victory Point if you have at least one Command Support remaining at the end of the game.

specialRules.name: Uncovering the Relic
specialRules.definition: Only one of the Objective markers is actually the relic that both sides seek. The first time each turn an unengaged Infantry model ends its movement in base contact with an Objective, they may search it in an attempt to uncover the relic. When this happens, flip over the marker. If it is marked, then the relic has been discovered and the model that discovered it takes possession of it. If it is unmarked then the relic is not there, remove the Objective from play.

specialRules.name: Inside Info
specialRules.definition: The Underdog player automatically wins the roll for choosing the priority in the first turn.

scenarios.name: Hoard of Treasures
scenarios.description: There are many sites in Middle-earth where ancient kings have been laid to rest, often alongside vast hoards of gold. However, extracting such riches from their resting place can be difficult, especially in the midst of battle!
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65. Then, place three Objective Markers in each half of the board/ The first is placed exactly 18" from the centre of one player's board edge. The others are then placed halfway between the central objective and the board edges on either side, ensuring that they are equidistant along an imaginary line 18" from one player's board edge (see map). These represent the Relics of Power.

If you have at least three models wholly within 12" of your opponent's board edge, then you instead score 2 Victory Points.

specialRules.name: Uncovering Artefacts
specialRules.definition:
The Objective Markers in a Scenario with this special rule represent artefacts and other valuable trinkets that must be uncovered. An Infantry model who is in base contact with an Objective Marker at the end of its Move may attempt to free it.

The model attempting to free the Artefact must take an Intelligence Test. If the test is passed, the Artefact has been freed and the model that freed it immediately takes possession of it: an Artefact is treated as a Light Object (see page 134 of the Middle-Earth Strategy Battle Game Rules Manual). Might cannot be used to influence this roll. Only one model from each side may attempt to uncover each Artefact each turn. Models may hold any number of Artefacts.

scenarios.startingPositions: Both players roll a D6 - the player with the highest result chooses one of the deployment zones. They then deploy wholly within 12" of the centre of their board edge. Models may not be deployed further than 6" from the Leader.

scenarios.name: Sites of Power
scenarios.description: There are many places across Middle-earth where old magic still clings to ancient sites. Although their power has waned, the protective wards that remain are still potent enough to deflect an arrow or turn aside a deadly blow.

scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65. Then, place four Objective Markers on the battlefield. The first Objective Marker is placed exactly halfway between the centre of the board and the north-east corner of the board edge. The other three Objective Markers are deployed in the same way in relation to the south-east, south-west, and north-west corners respectively (See map).

scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65.
scenarios.objectives: The game ends at the end of the turn when either the target Hero is slain, or one Battle Company is reduced to less than 25% of its starting numbers.

rewards.name: Survival of the Fittest

scoring.item: of your Hero models within 3" of the centre of the board

options.text: You score 1 Victory Point for each of your Hero models within 3" of the centre of the board at the end of the game, to a maximum of 3 Victory Points.

Each player splits their Battle Company into two halves of as close of a Rating as possible. The half that contains the Leader will be considered Primary force.

Both players then roll a D6 - the player that scored highest becomes Team A and choose one of the deployment zones in the centre of the board. Team A then deploys their Primary Force wholly within 6" of the centerline of the board in their deployment zone. Team B then deploys similarly. Once both Primary Forces have been deployed, Team A deploys their Secondary Force within 6" of their opposing board edge, followed by Team B doing likewise.

scenarios.name: Stand Your Ground
scenarios.description: One company has found themselves atop a hill, a highly advantageous position if they can keep it. Yet enemy forces desire it, not only to deny it to their foes but to seize its strategic value for themselves.
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65. In the centre of the board there should be a hill with a diameter of no larger than 12".
scenarios.objectives:
The Defender has been tasked with keeping the hill at all costs, whilst the Attacker must take it for their cause.

The game lasts until the end of the 8th Turn.

Some Victory Points will be scored during the course of play rather than solely at the end.

options.text: At the end of each turn after the first, you score 1 Victory Point if you have the more models within the outpost as your opponent.
If you have twice as many models as your opponent, you instead score 2 Victory Points.
You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Leader was wounded during the game.
If the enemy Leader was removed as a casualty, you instead score 2 Victory Points.
You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Battle Company is Broken at the end of the game.
If the enemy Battle Company is Broken and your Battle Company is not, you instead score 2 Victory Points.

specialRules.name: Defend the Hill
specialRules.definition: Models on the hill do not need to take Courage tests for being Broken.

scenarios.startingPositions: If there is a difference of 25 rating or more between both companies (excluding Against the Odds), the player with the lower rated company may choose who is the Attacker and Defender. Otherwise, both players roll a D6, with the lowest scoring player becoming the Defender. The Defender deploys their Battle Company anywhere upon the hill. The Attacker may then deploy their Battle Company anywhere at least 6" away from the hill.

scenarios.name: Defend the Gate
scenarios.description: Your company has been tasked with protecting the gates of an allied stronghold, and preventing anyone else from entering. As they guard the gates, an enemy Battle Company has been commanded to break through and claim the stronghold, giving their lord a crucial strategic advantage in the wars to come.
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout:
Set up terrain as described on page 65. Then, place a gate on one board edge. This gate should be 12" across.

Within 12" of the centre of the gate, there should be a few moderately defensible positions for the Defenders to make use of. These could be anything from barricades to difficult terrain. Rohirrim palisades, watch-towers, and the pallisade-gate (opened) make great terrain for this purpose, just make sure it isn't a full-scale siege!
scenarios.objectives:
The defending player must try to defend the gate by having their Battle Company within 6" of it, whilst keeping the Attacker at bay.

Once one Battle Company has been Broken, the game may suddenly end. At the end of each turn after this condition has been met, roll a D6. On a 1-2 the game ends, otherwise it continues for another turn.

options.text: You score 4 Victory Points if you have more models within 6" of the objective than your opponent.
If you have twice as many models within 6" of the objective than your opponent, then you instead score 8 Victory Points.
If you have three times as many models within 6" of the objective than your opponent, or you are the only player to have models within 6" of the objective, then you instead score 12 Victory Points.

If the enemy Leader was removed as a casualty, you instead score 3 Victory Points.

specialRules.name: Let nothing through!
specialRules.definition: Models from the Defender's Battle Company automatically pass all Courage tests they are required to make whilst within 6" of the Gate.

Otherwise, Both players roll a D6, with the player who scored lowest becoming the Defender. The Defender deploys their Battle Company within 6" of the gate as shown on the map. The Attacker then places their entire Battle Company within 24" of the southern board edge.

scenarios.name: Hold the Line
scenarios.description: One Battle Company has been tasked with guarding a path, mountain pass or similar, preventing anyone from passing through. A rival Battle Company is in desperate need of using the path in order to meet with the rest of their allies, and will have to fight their way through in order to reach them.
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65. The board should have a path running through the centre of it from north to south.
scenarios.objectives: The attacking Battle Company must have as many of their models escape the board via the northern board edge, whilst the Defenders must attempt to prevent them. Once the Attacker has been Broken, the game may suddenly end. At the end of each turn after this condition has been met, roll a D6. On a 1-2 the game ends, otherwise it continues for another turn.

options.text: The Attacker earns 4 Victory Points if any of their models have escaped the battlefield via the Northern board edge.
If at least half of the Attacker's models successfully escape the battlefield, they instead earn 8 Victory Points.
If all of the Attacker's models escape the battlefield, the Attacker instead earns 12 Victory Points.

scoring.item: Attacking Hero model removed as a casualty

options.text: The Defender earns 2 Victory Points for each Attacking Hero model they remove as a casualty, up to a maximum of 6 Victory Points.

If the enemy Leader was removed as a casualty, you instead score 3 Victory Points.

If the Attacker's Battle Company is Broken and the Defender's Battle Company is not, they instead score 6 Victory Points.

scenarios.name: Baggage Train

Yet such a cargo can attract those with dastardly plans, intent on ambushing and stealing the spoils for themselves. Suddenly, one company finds themselves ambushed and surrounded, and must fight to keep hold of what is rightfully theirs.
scenarios.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarios.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65.
scenarios.objectives:
The Defender is trying to escape to safety with as many of their Baggage Ponies as possible. The Attacker is trying to prevent the Defender from doing so, and in return claim the cargo for themselves.

Once there are no Baggage Ponies on the board, the game might suddenly end. At the end of each turn after this condition has been met, roll a D6. On the result of 1-2, the game ends – otherwise, the battle continues for another turn!

rewards.name: Cargo
rewards.text: If either side scores all Cargo, whether by possessing it or escaping with it, then that Company earns 1 bonus Influence.

condition.label: Scored all Cargo (possessing it or escaping with it)

options.text: For each piece of Cargo being held by the Defenders or on a Bagge Pony, they earn 1 Victory Points.
For each Cargo that the Defender moves any off the board, they instead earn 3 Victory Points.
For each Cargo not held by any model or Pony, the Attackers earn 1 Victory Point.

specialRules.name: Baggage Ponies
specialRules.definition:
